text.p: Bulgaria, grappling with soaring inflation, on Monday announced plans to issue a 20,000-lev note, the next largest denomination after current 10,000-lev notes.

"The government today approved the design of a 20,000-lev note proposed by the central bank," a government press centre official told reporters. He declined to say when the new note was expected to be put in circulation.

Soaring inflation measured at 2,041 percent year on year in March has made higher denominations necessary to make large payments easier and to cut the cost of maintaining the volume of money in circulation.
The new note would be worth $12.66 at Monday's spot rate of 1,580 levs per dollar.
The interim government in February approved the design of a 50,000-lev note expected to go into circulation by end-June.
A 100,000 lev-note, the largest denomination planned so far, was approved this month and was expected to be put in circulation in the autumn.
Levs in circulation rose to 311 billion levs on April 11 from 272 billion levs a week earlier and 127 billion levs at end-1996, preliminary central bank figures showed.
Under a memorandum of economic policies agreed with the International Monetary Fund (IMF) annual inflation for this year was projected at 769 percent and at 14 percent for next year.
Monthly inflation for March was 12.3 percent and cumulative inflation for the first quarter was 452.3 percent. Annual inflation for 1996 was 311 percent.
Monthly inflation rate for April was projected below last month's level, a National Statistics Institute official said. -- Sofia Newsroom, (++359-2) 91188
